h1: Stucco Painting Calgary: Acrylic Recoats and Re-Stucco
heroSub: Painting, acrylic recoats and full re-stucco across Calgary, Airdrie, Chestermere, Cochrane and Okotoks, explained by system, scope and season. Call (403) 555-0148 to be put in touch with an independent stucco contractor for a no-obligation quote.
introHtml:
Stucco painting in Calgary is one of three ways to bring a tired wall back: paint or coat it to refresh the colour, recoat it with an acrylic finish, or re-stucco it over a properly prepared base. Which one fits depends on what the wall is made of, how sound the base coat is and whether water has been getting in behind it. An independent stucco contractor works that out on site before anyone names a price.

This page explains the differences in plain terms: cement stucco, acrylic finish and EIFS, what cold weather does to the schedule, and what a written quote should spell out. Sandstone Stucco Co is advertising paid for by independent stucco contractors. The contractor who quotes your job contracts directly with you, and every price below is attributed to the firm that published it. For smaller jobs, see stucco repair in Calgary and the stucco repair cost page.

sections.heading: Painting, acrylic recoat or re-stucco: three scopes
sections.html:
The three scopes differ in how much of the wall the contractor opens up. A coating or paint refresh treats the surface, an acrylic recoat replaces the finish layer over a base that is still sound, and a re-stucco removes and rebuilds part or all of the system. Contractors usually settle the scope after walking the wall because, as Calgary Stucco and Slate puts it, nobody can tell you the full extent of water damage until the wall is opened up.

  • Stucco painting or a liquid coat: refreshes colour on a wall that is otherwise sound. It sits on the outside, so cracks, soft spots and staining are looked at before colour is chosen.
  • Acrylic recoat: a new acrylic finish over prepared stucco, usually after patching and crack work are done.
  • Re-stucco: stucco taken back to the sheathing or paper, then paper, mesh, base coats and finish rebuilt. Total Exteriors describes this route for widespread damage, extensive moisture problems or stucco beyond its natural lifespan, which that firm puts at 40 to 50 years.

If the trouble is a few cracks or holes rather than the whole finish, start with stucco repair. Cracking at the base of the wall is covered under parging, and hail or flicker marks on the hail and woodpecker damage page.

sections.heading: Cement, acrylic and EIFS in plain terms
sections.html:
Traditional cement stucco is built in coats on mesh. Imasco's 2024 guide specification for a three-coat system calls for a scratch coat of at least 10 mm, a brown coat of no more than 10 mm, and a combined system thickness of 19 mm, with a finish coat on top. It is a hard mineral wall, and Imasco notes that some cracking and efflorescence are inherent to portland cement.

Acrylic finish is a different finish coat, usually over the same cement base. Calgary Parging reported in 2024 that cement stucco with an acrylic finish was the choice on over 87% of the residential properties it worked on, which is that firm's own job mix and not a city survey. Martini Stone Masonry says acrylic stays flexible through freeze-thaw and holds colour without repainting; that is a contractor claim to test against the quote in front of you.

EIFS is a different build: foam insulation board with a basecoat, mesh and finish over it. One job on Martini's Calgary cost page lists a membrane, 1.5-inch foam, ADEX basecoat, primer and finish. Calgary Parging says woodpeckers are drawn to EIFS because the foam behind the finish is softer than concrete and sounds hollow, so raise flicker damage with the contractor if your wall is EIFS.

sections.heading: Prep, curing and cold-weather limits
sections.html:
Temperature sets the schedule more than the calendar does. Imasco's guide specification says to do no stucco work when air and substrate temperatures are below 4°C or above 38°C for 24 hours before, during and after application. ADEX asks for at or above 5°C for at least 24 hours for its base coat and for its CRYSTAL acrylic liquid coat. Calgary Parging says stucco cures best above 5°C in dry conditions, typically April through October, and that off-season work needs heated hoarding.

Fresh cement work also has to cure before it is coated. ADEX's bulletin for CRYSTAL requires a mandatory one-month cure for cement-based substrates before that liquid coat goes on, and Imasco says its cement finish may go on after a minimum of 7 days in ideal conditions. Calgary Stucco and Slate says some repairs take two trips and some up to four, with up to weeks in between so each layer cures. Ask which product data sheet your contractor's schedule follows.

Colour is the other limit. Imasco says colour can vary with weather, texture, job conditions and method of application, and that one colour batch number should cover the whole job. Calgary Parging says that on heavily weathered or discontinued finishes it will say upfront if a perfect match is not achievable, and offers refinishing a full elevation instead of chasing an invisible patch. So a whole-elevation recoat can be worth pricing alongside the patch.

sections.heading: Prices, permits and what a written quote should say
sections.html:
The sources behind this page give no Calgary price for stucco painting, and Calgary Parging's own painting page offers a quote after looking at the wall rather than a figure. So the contractor quotes painting once the wall has been seen. For recoats and re-stucco, these are the published figures, each from the firm named:

  • Calgary Stucco and Slate, framed as a very rough guide: full exterior re-coats or re-stuccos around $5,000 to $20,000 and up (GST not stated).
  • Martini Stone Masonry, on a cost page drawn from Calgary, Cochrane, Priddis and Canmore jobs: one elevation with brick stripped and an acrylic finish $14,350, and full applications $14.50 to $18 per square foot plus $4.50 per square foot where cement board is needed (all ex GST).
  • Calgary Parging, 2024 price list: acrylic stucco for a bungalow $12,000 to $18,000 and a mid-size house $18,000 to $33,000 (GST not stated).
  • Total Exteriors, August 2025: full stucco replacement $25 to $50 per square foot (GST not stated).
  • Calgary Parging: scaffolding for upper-storey or peaked sections typically $4,000 to $12,900 (ex GST).
  • Martini Stone Masonry: siding removed and replaced with an EIFS system $36,800 (ex GST).

On permits, the City of Calgary says most repair or replacement work does not need a development or building permit, and that replacing exterior cladding with a similar material that performs as well or better is allowed. A building permit is listed for siding with a different material, and development and building permits for larger or smaller windows or doors. Stucco is not named on the City's storm-damage page, so confirm your own project with the City on 311.

For a quote you can hold a contractor to, ask for the system by name (three-coat cement, acrylic finish or EIFS), the base coat and finish products, the prep and any sheathing or paper work, scaffolding, the colour and batch plan, the temperature and cure conditions the schedule assumes, and whether the total includes GST. Alberta advises a written contract, more than one written estimate and confirming Workers' Compensation Board coverage. Where money is paid before the work is finished, the prepaid contracting regulation says a contract over $200 must set out the types of materials and the work to be carried out.

faq.q: Can stucco be painted in Calgary, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Independent Calgary contractors quote stucco painting and liquid coatings after seeing the wall. No Calgary painting price is published in the sources behind this page, so none is given here. Upper-storey or peaked sections may need scaffolding, which Calgary Parging puts at typically $4,000 to $12,900 (ex GST), so ask whether it is in the quote.

faq.q: How much does a full recoat or re-stucco cost in Calgary?
faq.a: Calgary Stucco and Slate gives a very rough guide of around $5,000 to $20,000 and up for full exterior re-coats or re-stuccos, GST not stated. Martini Stone Masonry lists one elevation with brick stripped and an acrylic finish at $14,350 ex GST, and Calgary Parging's 2024 list has acrylic stucco for a mid-size house at $18,000 to $33,000. These are individual firms' figures, not a Calgary average, so a quote depends on wall area, access and what is found behind the stucco.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to re-stucco or recoat my house?
faq.a: The City of Calgary says most repair or replacement work does not need a development or building permit, and replacing cladding with a similar material is allowed. A building permit is listed for siding in a different material, and development and building permits for larger or smaller windows or doors. Call 311 to confirm your project, and to check that the contractor holds a valid City of Calgary business licence.

faq.q: What temperature does stucco need for a recoat?
faq.a: Imasco's guide specification says no stucco work below 4°C or above 38°C for 24 hours before, during and after application. ADEX asks for 5°C or higher for at least 24 hours for its base coat and its acrylic liquid coat. Calgary Parging says stucco cures best above 5°C, typically April through October, and ADEX requires new cement-based stucco to cure for one month before CRYSTAL liquid coat goes on.

faq.q: Who does the work, and who am I contracting with?
faq.a: Sandstone Stucco Co is advertising paid for by independent stucco contractors. It does no stucco work, holds no trade licence or warranty and does not handle insurance claims, and the contractor who quotes your job contracts directly with you. Alberta advises a written contract, more than one written estimate and confirming WCB coverage. If hail is involved, the City of Calgary says to contact your home insurance provider before any repair work.
